steps.title: Overview
steps.html:
There are 2 operating levels of the mine currently - Polyhalite and Salt. 


The diagram below shows the position of the different rock units at the mine and the mine infrastructure.
It also shows the potential major hazards associated with the geology of these areas.

steps.title: Polyhalite Mining Geology-1
steps.html:
• The current mining area for Polyhalite is referred to as Zone 1. Below is the generalised structure of the geology of Zone 1. 
  • The polyhalite seam is around 15m thick but varies across Zone 1.  
  • The Polyhalite seam has been characterised into 3 layers termed P1, P2 and P3, with P1 at the top and P3 at the bottom
  • The lower P3 Polyhalite is the highest grade. The target mining horizon is typically 3-5m above the base of seam
  • P2 has more salt bands which get thicker the higher up you go, until the ultimate roof of the polyhalite is Salt.
  • P1 is around 1m thick and is not relevant to mining.

images.caption: Schematic cross-section through the Zone 1 Polyhalite Geology

steps.title: Polyhalite Mining Geology-2
steps.html:
• In general, the higher the mining is above base of seam, the higher the amount of halite (salt) that is present which reduces the quality of the ore and can pose a risk to ground condition as salt is geotechnically weaker than polyhalite.
  • Lower in the seam, this halite is present as thin but continuous bands which pinch and swell (P3 Polyhalite). Higher in the seam, the halite bands become thicker and more frequent (P2 Polyhalite), until eventually the top of seam which is in the “Z2” halite.
  • The salt bands often have a clay/shale margin above and below the salt. This can form a plane of weakness which can result in delamination and roof issues (ripping).
